about: Every source tried for the 2026 general (WA, CA, CO): what it gives us, whether our robots-checked fetcher (comparison-builders/build.py fetch) may use it, and which builder reads it. Start a new election here: look for the same kind of source in the new state. `python3 tools/source-check.py` re-checks access for every entry. access: ok | robots-disallow (robots.txt blocks Claude-User) | robots-403 (robots.txt unreadable, so treated as a block) | http-403 (blocks plain fetches; never work around it) | robots-400 (robots.txt answers 400; treated as a block) | none-found. Our rule (cb.robots_allow) needs Claude-User allowed, the agent the fetcher identifies as. Since 2026-10-27, blocks on only the ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai crawler agents (common on news and state sites) don't count: these are user-requested fetches, not crawls.

kinds.ballot: Who and what is on the ballot, in printed order (official)
kinds.statements: Candidates' own statements (official voters' pamphlet / guide)
kinds.measure-text: Measure summaries, fiscal impact, what a yes/no vote means (official)
kinds.judicial-evaluation: An official body's evaluation of judges on retention questions
kinds.judicial-bio: A court's own biography of a judge
kinds.bar-rating: A bar association's rating of judicial candidates
kinds.news-guide: A news outlet's voter guide or candidate coverage
kinds.slate: A party, newspaper editorial board, League of Women Voters or advocacy group's picks
kinds.office-duties: What an office does, from the office's own site or the state's voter guide

sources.name: CA Secretary of State Official Voter Information Guide
sources.notes: Proposition pages: summary, fiscal impact, what your vote means (ca-props.json, built earlier). robots.txt returned 403 on 2026-10-27, so a re-run would refuse.

sources.name: CA SOS voter guide PDFs (vig.cdn.sos.ca.gov)
sources.notes: robots.txt returns S3 AccessDenied (2026-10-27), which our fetcher treats as a block. The candidate statements PDF in the cache predates that check: decide whether a missing-file 403 on a CDN counts as a block.

sources.name: LA County Interactive Sample Ballot data
sources.notes: Sample ballots are per voter; the ISB JSON gives each ballot style.

sources.name: California Supreme Court and Court of Appeal justices' biographies
sources.notes: No official retention evaluation exists that we found. Bios of recent appointees quote the Judicial Nominees Evaluation Commission rating (10/18). Supreme Court list: https://supreme.courts.ca.gov/ . Confirmation releases on courts.ca.gov / newsroom.courts.ca.gov also allowed.

sources.name: Los Angeles County Bar Association judicial ratings
sources.notes: Every LAist-reported rating is checked against it.

sources.name: LAist voter guides
sources.notes: Per-race guides, statewide ones by CalMatters. Doesn't cover U.S. House 28 or Monterey Park city races.

sources.name: CalMatters voter guide
sources.notes: Proposition explainer videos on its YouTube channel; Supreme Court retention page.

sources.name: State Bar of California attorney search
FPPC enforcement releases
sources.notes: Monthly releases since 2021, searched by name.

sources.name: California Democratic / Republican Party, LWV California
sources.notes: cadem.org pages 403 to plain fetches; its PDF and the Riverside County Democratic Party relay work.

sources.name: Los Angeles Times editorial board
sources.notes: Allows Claude-User. Anthropic's WebSearch can't search latimes.com, so find editorials from latimes.com/opinion and latimes.com/topic/editorials (that list was stale on 2026-10-27). Only one 2026 ballot editorial was linked there (no on Prop 40).

sources.name: SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Press Democrat, SCNG papers (Daily News, SGV Tribune, Register)
sources.notes: Still block Claude-User in robots.txt (2026-10-27). Sacramento Bee: robots-403. The LA Times is its own entry.

sources.name: counciloris council-meeting clips (our own transcriber)
sources.notes: Officeholders and public commenters only; challengers have none.

sources.name: CO SOS certified candidate list
sources.notes: robots.txt now disallows ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai (2026-10-27); the bundle was built from it earlier. The county sample ballot covers the same names.

sources.name: Colorado Blue Book (Legislative Council)
sources.notes: The legislature's judicial evaluations PDF there was still the 2024 edition on 2026-10-27; use the OJPE site.

sources.name: Larimer County sample ballot
sources.notes: Fetched fine on 2026-10-20; plain fetches got 403 on 2026-10-27, so re-use the parsed sample-ballots/larimer.json.

sources.name: Colorado Office of Judicial Performance Evaluation
sources.notes: Our honest research user agent is served; WebFetch and curl's default agent get a CloudFront 403 (don't impersonate a browser to get past that). Every judge on the ballot, official recommendation + vote + narrative.

sources.name: League of Women Voters VOTE411
sources.notes: Terms forbid automated access and copying: link each race, never copy answers.

sources.name: Colorado Politics
sources.notes: No editorial board slate. Columnists Tom Cronin and Bob Loevy publish a shared 'Our take' column each fall with each writer's verdict on every statewide measure; search 'Cronin Loevy our take ballot measures'. Many verdicts are bare ('CRONIN: Against.'), so co.py checks each against its measure's section. Also a news 'Judicial retention' explainer and guest columns (opinion, not used).

sources.name: Denver Post, Colorado Sun
sources.notes: Coloradoan and LWV Colorado: robots-403. Colorado Politics is its own entry.

sources.name: Colorado Public Radio
sources.notes: Purplish ballot-measure episodes on YouTube (videos stay usable). robots.txt now disallows ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai (2026-10-27); quiz-builders fetched its articles earlier, so re-running them would now refuse.

sources.name: PolitiFact personality pages
sources.notes: robots.txt crawl delay 10 s, kept. Only pages whose bio names the state.

sources.name: Ballotpedia
sources.notes: Was blocking automated access earlier in October; on 2026-10-27 our research user agent got a page. Use it to orient (who's running, which races), and take facts from the official source it cites.

sources.name: Census geocoder + state redistricting files
sources.notes: Check a handful of real addresses per city: CA's Prop 50 map moved Monterey Park to CA-28.

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb
sources.notes: District maps for every state: Legislative/MapServer has the 120th Congress (layer 0) and 2026 state legislative districts (1 upper, 2 lower), Jan 1 2026 vintage. Also city limits (Places .../4), primary roads, areal water. The Census geocoder names the same layers, so districts.py checks real addresses against the drawn shapes. Has no city council, county council or school districts.

sources.name: ArcGIS Online hosted layers (services.arcgis.com)
sources.notes: Where most city and county open-data portals serve their layers (Seattle council districts ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/Seattle_City_Council_Districts; King County council kccdst_wtrbdy on Ej0PsM5Aw677QF1W). Its robots.txt returns 400 'Invalid URL', which our rule counts as a block (only 404 counts as no robots.txt) — pending the user's decision (2026-10-27). King County's own gismaps.kingcounty.gov disallows /arcgis/.

sources.name: YouTube (oEmbed + yt-dlp)
sources.notes: yt-dlp needs the curl-cffi extra (pip install 'yt-dlp[default,curl-cffi]') for --impersonate; captions 429 from home IP, so download audio and transcribe with mlx_whisper.

sources.name: CA Secretary of State, statewide office descriptions (June 2010 voter guide, archived)
sources.notes: Covers every CA statewide office. The current guide (voterguide.sos.ca.gov) robots-blocks Claude-User; the archive host allows it. Only the 2010 edition exists in the archive; BOE's tax list there is out of date, so BOE uses boe.ca.gov.
